title: The <algorithm> functions worth knowing
summary: lower_bound, upper_bound, accumulate, max_element, reverse, iota, fill, unique and next_permutation — what each does and what it costs.

sections.title: The list
sections.body:
| Function | Does | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `lower_bound(b, e, x)` | iterator to first ≥ x in a **sorted** range | O(log n) |
| `upper_bound(b, e, x)` | first > x | O(log n) |
| `accumulate(b, e, 0LL)` | sum (use `0LL` to sum in long long!) | O(n) |
| `*max_element(b, e)` / `min_element` | largest / smallest value | O(n) |
| `reverse(b, e)` | reverse in place | O(n) |
| `iota(b, e, 0)` | fill 0, 1, 2, … | O(n) |
| `fill(b, e, v)` | fill with v | O(n) |
| `unique(b, e)` | removes **adjacent** duplicates, returns new end | O(n) |
| `next_permutation(b, e)` | next lexicographic order, false at the end | O(n) |
| `count(b, e, x)` | occurrences of x | O(n) |

sections.title: Turning an iterator into an index
sections.body: ✍️ `int idx = lower_bound(a.begin(), a.end(), x) - a.begin();` — if `idx == n`, every element is < x.

sections.title: The unique idiom
sections.body:
```cpp
sort(a.begin(), a.end());
a.erase(unique(a.begin(), a.end()), a.end());   // a now has distinct values, sorted
```
`unique` only removes *adjacent* duplicates, which is why you sort first.

sections.title: The accumulate trap
sections.body: ✍️ `accumulate(a.begin(), a.end(), 0)` sums in `int` because the initial value is `int` — it overflows on large inputs. Write `0LL`.
